title: Recomposition: what triggers it, and how to avoid the wasteful kind

videos.script: Compose runs your composables again whenever something they read changes. This lesson stops guessing about that and counts it. {{triggers}} A screen with a title, a total and a button. Three clicks. The title runs once and the total runs four times, and you will see exactly why. {{skipping}} Then skipping. Compose compares the arguments of each call with last time's. An equal list is skipped. A new object with a var inside is never skipped. {{reports}} Then the compiler's own report, which names the field that made the planner's session unstable. It is the date. One line in a file fixes that, and the report agrees. {{derived}} Then a goal banner. Fourteen changes to the minutes, and a derived value that changes once. {{keys}} And last, keys, because without them the rows of a list keep each other's memory.
